agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: REUSE was tried first and exhausted against real artifacts: the observation already carried every element (107 on email-inbox) and the existing compilers were read -- the contract compiler refused with MULTI_APP before any clause was built, so no existing path could name a row; the descriptor resolver resolves a DESCRIBED target by attribute but has no notion of containment, so it cannot say 'the control inside the record named X'. ADAPT was rejected because adapting the descriptor's version space to records would have introduced a second resolver with its own vocabulary, which is exactly the one-entry-per-app route this receipt refuses.
agent_orientation.what_this_is_not: Not a claim of sentience, not a benchmark rank, not a capability or weight credit. It is a coordinate language for one observation plus the measurement that it converts pages.
agent_orientation.independent_verification_note: Producer-run sandbox only. Independent personnel verification is still open.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: Speculative forecast only: naming a region of an observation is the cheapest currently available prerequisite to any later work that must say 'that one'. No obligation discharge, benchmark gain, capability credit or independent verification is claimed.

recursive_obs.real_outcome: Six email pages that three rounds of refusal had called 'state outside the observation' now resolve from the instruction alone: open the named record, write the quoted text, press the control the sentence names -- with the page's reward read only afterwards.
recursive_obs.required_capability: Naming the region of an observation that a word picks out, and proving by name when it cannot: more than one record matches, the record holds no such control, no element shows the identifier, or the record is reachable but not present.
routes_considered: One vocabulary entry per app (email, contacts, calendar) -- rejected: the frame is one coordinate change and serves every record-shaped page
Walk from the identifier to the nearest ancestor holding any two controls -- measured wrong: that ancestor is div.email-left and the star is in the sibling div.email-right
Match identity on full_text -- measured wrong: every ancestor of a name then shows the name and one email looks like seven records
Match a control by class prefix -- measured wrong: email-sender starts with 'email'
Match a control by exact class/id token plus the sentence's own verb -- measured right on send-reply, send-forward, trash, star

recursive_obs.self_model_claim: It can name what it can name, and it says so when it cannot. No further claim is made.

obs_goal.real_outcome: A word in the instruction names one region of one observation, and the machine can act inside that region -- or refuse by name when it cannot.

obs_solution.generality_mechanism: One coordinate change -- (container, identifier, path_from_id) -- serves every record-shaped page, because 'the star of that row' is not an email fact. No app is named anywhere in the module.
obs_solution.efficiency_mechanism: The frame is re-derived from the live observation on every action; nothing is stored between pages, and a clause already satisfied by construction costs no action.
obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Nearest-ancestor-holding-any-control was measured wrong (it stops at div.email-left while the star is in the sibling div.email-right); full_text identity was measured wrong (every ancestor then shows the name); class-prefix control matching was measured wrong (email-sender starts with 'email'); compiling the value once at time zero was measured wrong (the field does not exist yet).
